title: Let a session recover project memories after a context refresh without paging the full listing each time
outcome: Let a session recover project memories after a context refresh without paging the full listing each time
acceptance: The memories line of a peek or next names the project memory keys changed since this session's recorded memory position, at most a fixed number of them, marks a forgotten key as forgotten, and gives the count and the listing command when more changed.
The recovery listing that a peek directs a session to reaches every one of several hundred project memories in a small number of reads, and a test on such a store counts those reads.
After a new context generation, a peek directs the session to list every current project memory key, whether or not any key changed and whether or not the session listed them before.
Plain `engram work memories --json` keeps its current row shape, including each row's remembered_at and actor_id.

completion.summary: After a context refresh, the memories line of next and peek names the keys changed since the session's recorded memory position: up to 8, newest first, forgotten ones marked, with the count and the listing command when more changed. A memories listing that carries the context generation is a compact recovery listing: key, revision and first-line preview, in pages fitted to the response budget, with continuations that keep the generation. 300 memories take at most 6 reads instead of 15. A new context is still directed to list every key. Plain memories and --json are unchanged. There is no schema change; a memory-state rebuild clears the recorded positions. Landed as 6be107c8 after a clean round-2 pair and FULL PASS test-a7a803f3; acceptance evaluation d05447db passed 4/4. Lows are filed as w-20f5d98ee3d7 and w-a7d8521d6c90.
